records.source: Ὁ δὲ Σαῦλος ἔτι ἐμπνέων ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς τοῦ κυρίου, προσελθὼν τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ ᾐτήσατο παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολὰς εἰς Δαμασκὸν πρὸς τὰς συναγωγάς, ὅπως ἐάν τινας εὕρῃ τῆς ὁδοῦ ὄντας, ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, δεδεμένους ἀγάγῃ εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.
records.gloss: The but Saul still breathing threat and murder toward the disciples of the Lord, having gone to the high priest \v 2 asked from him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, so that if any he found of the Way being, men both and women, having been bound he might bring [them] to Jerusalem.
pieces: Saul, however, still breathed threats and murder against the Lord's disciples. Going to the high priest,
he requested letters to the synagogues of Damascus. With them he could put in chains any people of the Way he found there, men and women alike, and take them back to Jerusalem.

L.1: But Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest
L.2: [and] asked from him letters to Damascus, to the synagogues, so that if he found any who were of the Way, both men and women, he might bring [them] bound to Jerusalem.

R.1: All this time Saul kept threatening to kill the Lord's followers. He went to the high priest.
R.2: He asked him for letters to the synagogues in the city of Damascus. Saul wanted to find people there who belonged to the Way, as the followers of Jesus were called. He wanted to arrest them, both men and women, and bring them back to Jerusalem as prisoners.

decisions.choice: but Saul, still: the story returns to Saul from 8:3
alternatives: a new episode with no link
decisions.reason: Saul was last seen ravaging the church in Jerusalem (8:1-3). Luke has followed Philip in between; "still" picks Saul up where he was left.

decisions.choice: breathing threat and murder: his whole being was set on threatening and killing the disciples
decisions.reason: Breath stands for what fills a person. Paul later says he persecuted the Way to the death and cast his vote against believers when they were put to death (22:4, 26:10).

decisions.choice: letters to the synagogues: the high priest's request that the Jewish communities of Damascus hand believers over
decisions.reason: The high priest had no power over the city of Damascus, in Syria, about 135 miles north-east of Jerusalem in a straight line. His letters asked the synagogues there to cooperate (22:5, 26:12).

decisions.choice: the Way: a name for the movement of those who follow Jesus
alternatives: a way of life in general
decisions.reason: Acts uses the word as a name for the believers and their teaching (19:9, 19:23, 22:4, 24:14, 24:22). It may echo "the way of the Lord" in Isaiah 40:3, which Luke 3:4 quotes of John the Baptizer.

decisions.choice: who belonged to the Way, as the followers of Jesus were called
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: the purpose clause as a separate sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the Greek sentence; the meaning is the same.

records.heading: Saul on the road to Damascus

records.source: ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐγγίζειν τῇ Δαμασκῷ, ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν φῶς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἤκουσεν φωνὴν λέγουσαν αὐτῷ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
records.gloss: In now the proceeding it came to pass him to draw near to Damascus, suddenly and him flashed around a light from heaven, \v 4 and having fallen on the ground he heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why me do you persecute?
pieces: On his way, as he was nearing Damascus, all at once a light from heaven blazed around him.
He dropped to the ground and heard a voice speaking to him: "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"

L.3: Now as he was going, it happened that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him,
L.4: and falling on the ground he heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"

R.3: Saul traveled on and came close to Damascus. Suddenly a bright light from heaven shone all around him.
R.4: He fell down to the ground. Then he heard a voice. It said to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you attacking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"

decisions.choice: flashed around: shone around him like lightning
decisions.reason: The verb is used of lightning. Paul's own accounts say it was a great light at about noon, brighter than the sun (22:6, 26:13).

decisions.choice: Saul, Saul: his name in its Hebrew form, called twice
alternatives: the Greek form of the name
decisions.reason: Luke's narrative uses the Greek form of the name; the voice uses the Hebrew form, and 26:14 says it spoke in the Hebrew language. God calls a name twice in Genesis 22:11, 46:2, Exodus 3:4 and 1 Samuel 3:10.

decisions.choice: persecuting me: to persecute the disciples is to persecute Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Saul was attacking the believers, yet the voice asks why he persecutes "me". Jesus counts what is done to his followers as done to him (Luke 10:16).

decisions.choice: attacking
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for hunting down and harming people.

records.source: εἶπεν δέ· Τίς εἶ, κύριε;
records.gloss: He said then, Who are you, Lord?
pieces: "Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?" he asked.

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect to a heavenly speaker, which the answer fills with its full sense
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite "sir" (16:30). Saul does not yet know who is speaking, but a light from heaven and a voice tell him he is facing a heavenly power. The answer, "I am Jesus", gives the word its full meaning.

decisions.choice: the deity pronoun setting on "you"
alternatives: no span, because Saul does not yet know who speaks
decisions.reason: The one addressed is the risen Jesus, so the pronoun takes the setting, as it does wherever Jesus is spoken to in Acts.

records.source: ὁ δέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·
records.gloss: The and [said], I am Jesus whom you persecute;
pieces: He answered, "I am Jesus, and you are persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.5: And he [said], "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

R.5: The voice answered, "I am Jesus. You are attacking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: and he: the speaker answers; the verb of saying is understood
decisions.reason: The Greek has only "and he"; the reply follows at once.

decisions.choice: I am Jesus: the one Saul persecutes is alive, speaking from heaven
alternatives: a vision with no real presence
decisions.reason: Saul thought Jesus was a dead man and his followers deceived. Paul later counts this as the risen Lord appearing to him (1 Corinthians 9:1, 15:8), and Ananias and Barnabas say he saw the Lord (9:17, 9:27).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: Jesus's words go straight on to "But get up" (9:6)
alternatives: the King James Version adds "it is hard for you to kick against the goads" and Saul's trembling question "Lord, what do you want me to do?"
decisions.reason: These added words have very little support in Greek manuscripts at this point. They appear in Latin witnesses and in the Greek text printed in the 1500s, and seem to have come from Paul's later accounts, where they belong: the goads in 26:14, the question in 22:10. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the voice
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker as Saul heard him.

decisions.choice: and you are persecuting me
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the relative clause a plain statement, as Jesus's charge to Saul.

records.source: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λαληθήσεταί σοι ὅ τί σε δεῖ ποιεῖν.
records.gloss: But rise up and enter into the city, and it will be told you what you it is necessary to do.
pieces: But get up and go into the city. There you will be told what you have to do."

L.6: But rise up and enter into the city, and it will be told you what you must do."

R.6: But get up and go into the city. Someone there will tell you what you must do."

decisions.choice: it will be told you: by someone not yet named
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the speaker open. 9:10-17 shows that the Lord sends Ananias, and 22:10-15 says Ananias told Saul what he was appointed to do.

decisions.choice: must: what God has purposed for Saul
decisions.reason: Luke often uses this word for what God has determined must happen (1:16, 3:21, 9:16).

decisions.choice: someone there will tell you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the passive a subject without naming who it will be.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἄνδρες οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτῷ εἱστήκεισαν ἐνεοί, ἀκούοντες μὲν τῆς φωνῆς μηδένα δὲ θεωροῦντες.
records.gloss: The and men the [ones] traveling with him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice, no one however seeing.
pieces: The men on the road with him stood there unable to speak. They heard the voice, but they saw no one.

L.7: And the men who were traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one.

R.7: The men who were traveling with Saul stood there. They were too shocked to say anything. They heard the voice, but they could not see anyone.

decisions.choice: the voice: the same voice that spoke to Saul
decisions.reason: The word means voice or sound; with the article it points back to the voice of 9:4. In Paul's own account in 22:9 the men with him saw the light but did not hear the voice of the one speaking to him. This account says they heard the voice but saw no one. Each passage is translated as it stands. The two may describe different sides of the event, such as hearing a sound without understanding words, but neither text explains how they fit together.

decisions.choice: seeing no one: they saw no person
decisions.reason: Saul saw the Lord (9:17, 9:27); his companions saw no one. In 22:9 they do see the light.

decisions.choice: speechless: struck dumb with fear or wonder
decisions.reason: The word describes people unable to speak for shock. In 26:14 they all fell to the ground.

decisions.choice: too shocked to say anything
decisions.reason: Readable says why they could not speak.

records.source: ἠγέρθη δὲ Σαῦλος ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἀνεῳγμένων δὲ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ οὐδὲν ἔβλεπεν· χειραγωγοῦντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
records.gloss: Rose up then Saul from the ground, having been opened however the eyes of him nothing he saw; leading by the hand then him they brought [him] into Damascus.
pieces: Saul rose from the ground. His eyes were open, yet he saw nothing at all, and his companions had to lead him by the hand into Damascus.

L.8: Then Saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were opened, he saw nothing; and leading him by the hand they brought [him] into Damascus.

R.8: Saul got up from the ground. His eyes were open, but he could not see anything. So the men took his hand and led him into the city of Damascus.

decisions.choice: his eyes were opened, yet he saw nothing: he was blind
decisions.reason: The contrast is between open eyes and no sight. Paul says in 22:11 that he could not see because of the brightness of the light.

decisions.choice: they: the men traveling with him
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; the men of 9:7 are the only others present.

decisions.choice: his companions; the men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who led him.

records.source: καὶ ἦν ἡμέρας τρεῖς μὴ βλέπων, καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲ ἔπιεν.
records.gloss: And he was days three not seeing, and not he ate nor drank.
pieces: He was without sight for three days, and all that time he neither ate nor drank.

L.9: And he was three days without seeing, and he neither ate nor drank.

R.9: Saul stayed blind for three days. During that time he did not eat or drink.

decisions.choice: he neither ate nor drank: a fast
alternatives: he had no appetite from shock
decisions.reason: The text does not say why. Fasting went with prayer and turning to God, and 9:11 says Saul was praying (compare 13:2-3, 14:23), but shock may also be part of it.

decisions.choice: three days without seeing: his blindness lasted three days
alternatives: he only kept his eyes shut
decisions.reason: The phrase continues 9:8. His sight returns in 9:18.

records.source: Ἦν δέ τις μαθητὴς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὀνόματι Ἁνανίας, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν ὁράματι ὁ κύριος· Ἁνανία.
records.gloss: There was now a certain disciple in Damascus by name Ananias, and said to him in a vision the Lord, Ananias.
pieces: Living in Damascus was a disciple by the name of Ananias. In a vision the Lord called him: "Ananias!"

L.10: Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias."

R.10: There was a follower of Jesus in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision. He said, "Ananias!"

decisions.choice: Ananias: a common Jewish name; not the Ananias of 5:1
decisions.reason: Paul later describes him as a devout man by the standard of the law, well spoken of by all the Jews living in Damascus (22:12).

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: In 9:17 Ananias says that the Lord who sent him is Jesus, who appeared to Saul on the road.

decisions.choice: a vision: something God shows a person, here with words spoken
decisions.reason: Acts uses the word for what is seen and heard from God, awake or asleep (10:3, 16:9, 18:9).

decisions.choice: a follower of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a disciple is.

records.heading: The Lord sends Ananias to Saul

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ, κύριε.
records.gloss: The and he said, Behold I, Lord.
pieces: "I am here, Lord," he answered.

R.10: Ananias answered, "Yes, Lord. I am listening."

decisions.choice: here I am: the reply of a servant ready to listen and obey
alternatives: a statement of where he was
decisions.reason: The same reply is given to God by Abraham (Genesis 22:1) and Samuel (1 Samuel 3:4).

decisions.choice: here
decisions.reason: The word points to the speaker himself; "here" is how English says it without an archaic word.

decisions.choice: Yes, Lord. I am listening
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ὁ δὲ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι ἐπὶ τὴν ῥύμην τὴν καλουμένην Εὐθεῖαν καὶ ζήτησον ἐν οἰκίᾳ Ἰούδα Σαῦλον ὀνόματι Ταρσέα, ἰδοὺ γὰρ προσεύχεται, καὶ εἶδεν ἄνδρα ἐν ὁράματι Ἁνανίαν ὀνόματι εἰσελθόντα καὶ ἐπιθέντα αὐτῷ χεῖρας ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃ.
records.gloss: The and Lord to him, Having risen up go to the street the [one] being called Straight and seek in [the] house of Judas Saul by name, of Tarsus; behold for he is praying, \v 12 and he saw a man in a vision, Ananias by name, having come in and having put on him hands so that he might see again.
pieces: The Lord said to him, "Get up and go to the street called Straight. There, at the house of Judas, look for a man of Tarsus by the name of Saul. Even now he is praying,
and he has seen a vision in which a man named Ananias comes in and lays his hands on him so that he can see again."

L.11: And the Lord [said] to him, "Get up [and] go to the street called Straight, and seek in [the] house of Judas [a man] named Saul, of Tarsus; for look, he is praying,
L.12: and he has seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in and laying hands on him so that he may see again."

R.11: The Lord said to him, "Get up and go to the street called Straight Street. Find the house of a man named Judas. Ask there for a man from the city of Tarsus. His name is Saul. He is praying right now.
R.12: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias. He saw Ananias come in and put his hands on him so that he could see again."

decisions.choice: the street called Straight: a main street of Damascus
alternatives: a description of any straight road
decisions.reason: Roman Damascus had a long, straight main street running east to west through the city; a street on its line is still there in the old city.

decisions.choice: of Tarsus: from Tarsus, a leading city of Cilicia
decisions.reason: Paul calls himself a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no unimportant city (21:39, 22:3).

decisions.choice: for he is praying: why Ananias will find him ready
alternatives: a mere report of what Saul is doing
decisions.reason: The word "for" gives the reason: Saul is praying, and God has already prepared him to receive Ananias (9:12).

decisions.choice: laying hands on him: a sign of blessing, here for healing
decisions.reason: Jesus laid hands on the sick (Luke 4:40), and so does Paul (28:8). In 9:17 the Holy Spirit is also given.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: The word calls for attention; "look" is modern English for it.

decisions.choice: short sentences, one step at a time
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the directions and the vision.

records.source: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ Ἁνανίας· Κύριε, ἤκουσα ἀπὸ πολλῶν περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τούτου, ὅσα κακὰ τοῖς ἁγίοις σου ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ·
records.gloss: Answered but Ananias, Lord, I have heard from many about the man this, how many evil things to the holy ones of you he did in Jerusalem;
pieces: But Ananias answered, "Lord, many have told me of this man, and of how much evil he did to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people in Jerusalem.

L.13: But Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy ones in Jerusalem;

R.13: But Ananias said, "Lord, many people have told me about this man. They say he did terrible things to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy people in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: your holy ones: the people who belong to the Lord, set apart for him
decisions.reason: This is the first time Acts uses the word for the believers (also 9:32, 9:41, 26:10). In the Old Testament Israel is a holy people (Exodus 19:6). "Your" makes them the Lord Jesus's own people.

decisions.choice: but: Ananias objects
decisions.reason: Ananias answers with what he knows of Saul, as if the Lord might not know it.

decisions.choice: holy people
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "holy ones"; Balanced and Readable say "holy people", as the letters to the Romans, Ephesians and Philippians do in this translation.

records.source: καὶ ὧδε ἔχει ἐξουσίαν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων δῆσαι πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομά σου.
records.gloss: and here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all those calling on the name of you.
pieces: Now he is here, and the chief priests have given him power to put in chains all who call on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."

L.14: and here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name."

R.14: Now he has come here to Damascus. The leading priests have given him the right to arrest everyone who prays to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: those who call on your name: those who pray to Jesus as Lord and belong to him
alternatives: those who say his name aloud
decisions.reason: Joel 2:32, quoted in 2:21, speaks of calling on the name of the Lord. Here the name is Jesus's (9:21, 22:16; 1 Corinthians 1:2).

decisions.choice: the chief priests: the high priest and the leading priestly families
decisions.reason: As in 4:23. In 9:1 Saul went to the high priest; here the whole priestly leadership stands behind him.

decisions.choice: bind: arrest and take prisoner
decisions.reason: As in 9:2 and 9:21, binding means taking people as prisoners.

decisions.choice: everyone who prays to you
alternatives: all who call on your name
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· Πορεύου, ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ἐστίν μοι οὗτος τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐνώπιον ἐθνῶν τε καὶ βασιλέων υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ, ἐγὼ γὰρ ὑποδείξω αὐτῷ ὅσα δεῖ αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματός μου παθεῖν.
records.gloss: Said however to him the Lord, Go, for a vessel of choice is to me this [man] to carry the name of me before Gentiles and also kings, sons also of Israel; \v 16 I for will show to him how many things it is necessary him for the name of me to suffer.
pieces: But the Lord told him, "Go, because I have chosen this man as a vessel to bear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name before Gentiles and kings and the people of Israel.
I myself will show him how much he will have to suffer for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name."

L.15: But the Lord said to him, "Go, for this [man] is a chosen vessel to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, to carry {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name before Gentiles and kings and [the] sons of Israel;
L.16: for I will show him how much he must suffer for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name."

R.15: But the Lord said to him, "Go! I have chosen this man to work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He will tell people about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He will speak to people who are not Jews, to kings, and to the people of Israel.
R.16: I will show him how much he must suffer for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: a chosen vessel: an instrument the Lord has picked for a task
decisions.reason: The word means a jar or a tool; "of choice" means chosen. Paul uses the picture of vessels in God's hand in Romans 9:21-23 and 2 Timothy 2:20-21.

decisions.choice: to carry my name: to make Jesus known and bear witness to him
alternatives: to bear the name of Christian
decisions.reason: Saul has been attacking those who call on the name (9:14); now he will carry it to others (9:20, 9:27-28).

decisions.choice: Gentiles, kings and Israel: those Saul will speak to
decisions.reason: Acts shows him speaking to Gentiles (13:46-48), to King Agrippa (26:1-29) and to his own people (13:16, 22:1).

decisions.choice: he must suffer: suffering is part of the calling
decisions.reason: "Must" is the word of God's purpose, as in 9:6. Paul later lists what he suffered (2 Corinthians 11:23-28), and tells believers that many troubles lie on the way into God's kingdom (14:22). The text does not call it punishment.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual Old Testament name for the whole nation.

decisions.choice: I have chosen this man
alternatives: this man is a chosen vessel to me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "of choice" into a verb with the Lord as subject, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: to work for me; tell people about me; people who are not Jews
alternatives: a chosen vessel; to carry my name; Gentiles
decisions.reason: Readable says what the images and the word Gentiles mean.

records.source: ἀπῆλθεν δὲ Ἁνανίας καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ ἐπιθεὶς ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ὁ κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με, Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἤρχου, ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃς καὶ πλησθῇς πνεύματος ἁγίου.
records.gloss: Went away then Ananias and entered into the house, and having laid on him the hands he said, Saul brother, the Lord has sent me, Jesus the [one] having appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that you may see again and be filled with [the] Spirit Holy.
pieces: So Ananias went off and entered the house. He put his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road you traveled, has sent me so that your sight may come back and you may be filled with the Holy Spirit."

L.17: Then Ananias went away and entered into the house, and laying [his] hands on him he said, "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me, Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that you may see again and be filled with [the] Holy Spirit."

R.17: So Ananias went to the house. He put his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus sent me. He is the one who showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to you on the road as you were coming here. He sent me so that you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, welcomed into the family of God's people
decisions.reason: Jews called one another brothers (2:29, 22:1), but Ananias has just learned that Saul is the Lord's chosen vessel; the word welcomes the former persecutor as one of the believers.

decisions.choice: the Lord ... Jesus: the name explains who the Lord is
decisions.reason: Ananias names the Lord who sent him as the Jesus Saul met on the road.

decisions.choice: appeared: was seen by you
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the risen Jesus appearing (13:31; 1 Corinthians 15:5-8). Saul saw him (9:27, 26:16).

decisions.choice: filled with the Holy Spirit: as the first believers were
decisions.reason: The believers were filled with the Spirit in 2:4 and 4:31. Luke does not say exactly when Saul was filled; 9:18 tells of his sight and his baptism.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus ... has sent me
alternatives: the Lord has sent me, Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring the name next to the title; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: a separate sentence: he is the one who showed himself to you
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up Ananias's words.

records.source: καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέπεσαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν ὡς λεπίδες, ἀνέβλεψέν τε καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη, καὶ λαβὼν τροφὴν ἐνίσχυσεν.
records.gloss: And immediately fell of him from the eyes [something] like scales, he saw again also, and having risen up he was baptized, \v 19 and having taken food he was strengthened.
pieces: All at once what looked like scales fell away from his eyes, and he could see. He stood up and was baptized;
then he took food and grew strong again.

L.18: And immediately [something] like scales fell from his eyes, and he saw again; and rising up he was baptized,
L.19: and taking food he was strengthened.

R.18: Right away, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes. He could see again. He got up and was baptized.
R.19: Then he ate some food and felt strong again.

decisions.choice: like scales: something like flakes; Luke says what it was like
decisions.reason: The word is used of fish scales and of flakes. Luke gives a comparison and does not name a condition.

decisions.choice: saw again: his sight came back
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 9:12 and 9:17: what the Lord promised happens.

decisions.choice: rising up he was baptized: at once, before he ate
decisions.reason: In 22:16 Ananias tells him to get up and be baptized without delay.

decisions.choice: Saul's eyes
decisions.reason: Readable names Saul to keep the people clear.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐν Δαμασκῷ μαθητῶν ἡμέρας τινὰς, καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: He was then with the in Damascus disciples days some, \v 20 and immediately in the synagogues he was proclaiming Jesus, that this one is the Son of God.
pieces: Saul stayed for some days with the disciples in Damascus.
Without delay he went into the synagogues and proclaimed Jesus, telling them that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Son of God.

L.19: And he was with the disciples in Damascus [for] some days,
L.20: and immediately in the synagogues he began proclaiming Jesus, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Son of God.

R.19: Saul stayed with the followers of Jesus in Damascus for several days.
R.20: Right away he began to go to the synagogues. He told the people there about Jesus. He told them that Jesus is the Son of God.

decisions.choice: the Son of God: Jesus's unique relation to God, and the promised King
decisions.reason: This is the only place Acts uses the title in these words; 13:33 applies Psalm 2:7 to Jesus. In Psalm 2:7 and 2 Samuel 7:14 the king of David's line is God's son, and Luke 1:32-35 calls Jesus Son of the Most High and Son of God. 9:22 sets beside it the claim that he is the Christ.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "Jesus"
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("he preached Christ in the synagogues"), have "Christ" here; the earliest manuscripts have "Jesus". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: was proclaiming: began and went on proclaiming
decisions.reason: The verb is in the imperfect, for something done again and again.

decisions.choice: Saul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Saul at the start of the scene.

decisions.choice: Jesus is the Son of God
alternatives: that he is the Son of God
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus instead of the pronoun.

records.heading: Saul proclaims Jesus in Damascus and Jerusalem

records.source: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πορθήσας ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο, καὶ ὧδε εἰς τοῦτο ἐληλύθει ἵνα δεδεμένους αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς;
records.gloss: Were amazed then all those hearing and were saying, Not this is the [one] having ravaged in Jerusalem those calling on the name this, and here for this he had come, that having been bound them he might bring to the chief priests?
pieces: All who heard him were astonished. "Is this not the man who tried to destroy those in Jerusalem who call on this name?" they said. "Did he not come here for this very purpose, to take them in chains to the chief priests?"

L.21: And all who heard were amazed and were saying, "Is this not the one who ravaged those in Jerusalem who call on this name, and had come here for this, that he might bring them bound to the chief priests?"

R.21: Everyone who heard him was amazed. They said, "This is the man who tried to destroy the people in Jerusalem who pray to Jesus! He came here to arrest people like that and take them to the leading priests."

decisions.choice: ravaged: tried to destroy
decisions.reason: Paul uses the same verb of himself in Galatians 1:13 and 1:23: he tried to destroy the church.

decisions.choice: is this not: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The hearers know who Saul is; they are amazed at the change.

decisions.choice: those who call on this name: the believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 9:14, calling on the name of Jesus marks those who belong to him.

decisions.choice: had come here: that was his purpose in coming
alternatives: he has now come for this
decisions.reason: The pluperfect looks back to why he came; the hearers see that he no longer acts on it.

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long question in two; both expect the answer yes.

decisions.choice: statements instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the question implies, and says whom they call on.

records.source: Σαῦλος δὲ μᾶλλον ἐνεδυναμοῦτο καὶ συνέχυννεν τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Δαμασκῷ, συμβιβάζων ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.
records.gloss: Saul however more was being empowered and was confounding the Jews those dwelling in Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
pieces: But Saul's power kept growing. He threw the Jews who lived in Damascus into confusion, demonstrating that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

L.22: But Saul was being strengthened all the more and was confounding the Jews who lived in Damascus, proving that this [one] is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.22: But Saul spoke with more and more power. The Jews who lived in Damascus could not argue against him. He showed them clearly that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: the Christ: a title, the Messiah, the anointed King God promised
decisions.reason: With the article and after "is", the word is a title, not a name: Saul argued that Jesus is the one Israel was waiting for, as in 17:3 and 18:5.

decisions.choice: proving: showing by putting the evidence together
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring together, and so to show by comparing. In 17:2-3 Paul does this from the Scriptures.

decisions.choice: was being strengthened: grew stronger in his speaking and conviction
decisions.reason: He had regained his bodily strength in 9:19; here the growth is in his preaching, as the rest of the sentence shows.

decisions.choice: confounding: leaving them confused and without an answer
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw into confusion (compare 2:6).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one meant.

decisions.choice: the Christ, with "the Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Here the word is a title, so it keeps the article.

records.source: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦντο ἡμέραι ἱκαναί, συνεβουλεύσαντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν·
records.gloss: When now were being fulfilled days many, plotted together the Jews to kill him;
pieces: After a good many days, the Jews made a plan to kill him.

L.23: Now when many days had passed, the Jews plotted together to kill him;

R.23: Many days later, the Jews in Damascus who were against Saul made plans to kill him.

decisions.choice: many days: a long time; Acts does not say how long
decisions.reason: Paul says that after his call he went away into Arabia, returned to Damascus, and only after three years went up to Jerusalem (Galatians 1:17-18). Acts does not mention Arabia; the two accounts are not told in the same detail.

decisions.choice: the Jews: Saul's Jewish opponents in Damascus
decisions.reason: Saul was a Jew, and so were the disciples there. The word here means those who rejected his preaching (9:22).

decisions.choice: the Jews in Damascus who were against Saul
decisions.reason: Readable says which Jews are meant, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ἐγνώσθη δὲ τῷ Σαύλῳ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: became known however to Saul the plot of them.
pieces: But Saul learned of their plot.

L.24: but their plot became known to Saul.

R.24: But Saul found out about their plan.

decisions.choice: became known: Saul was told of it; the text does not say by whom
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the source unnamed.

records.source: παρετηροῦντο δὲ καὶ τὰς πύλας ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀνέλωσιν·
records.gloss: They were watching closely also the gates day both and night so that him they might kill;
pieces: They were even guarding the gates around the clock, waiting for the chance to kill him.

L.24: And they were also watching the gates closely day and night so that they might kill him;

R.24: They watched the city gates day and night. They wanted to catch Saul and kill him.

decisions.choice: the gates: the gates in the city wall, the only ways out
decisions.reason: Damascus was a walled city. Watching its gates would catch Saul if he tried to leave.

decisions.choice: who watched: Acts names the Jews; Paul's own account names the governor
decisions.reason: In 2 Corinthians 11:32-33 Paul says that in Damascus the governor under King Aretas guarded the city to arrest him, and that he was let down in a basket through a window in the wall. Acts says the Jews watched the gates. Neither text says how the two fit together.

decisions.choice: around the clock
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English idiom for the Greek one.

records.source: λαβόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς διὰ τοῦ τείχους καθῆκαν αὐτὸν χαλάσαντες ἐν σπυρίδι.
records.gloss: having taken however the disciples of him by night through the wall they let down him, having lowered [him] in a basket.
pieces: One night, though, his disciples took him and got him out through the wall, letting him down in a basket.

L.25: But his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering [him] in a basket.

R.25: But one night Saul's followers helped him escape. They put him in a large basket. Then they let the basket down from an opening in the city wall.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "his disciples"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "the disciples took him"
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have "his disciples". Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "the disciples took him", which avoids giving Saul disciples of his own so soon. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: his disciples: people who had come to believe through Saul's preaching
alternatives: the believers of Damascus in general
decisions.reason: With the SBLGNT reading, these are people Saul had taught in Damascus. Luke elsewhere calls believers disciples of the Lord (9:1), so some take "his" loosely.

decisions.choice: through the wall: through an opening in it
decisions.reason: Paul says he was let down through a window in the wall (2 Corinthians 11:33). Houses were sometimes built into a city wall (Joshua 2:15).

decisions.choice: basket: a large basket of woven rope or reeds
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the large baskets of leftover food in Mark 8:8.

decisions.choice: from an opening in the city wall
decisions.reason: Readable says how it was done, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Παραγενόμενος δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐπείραζεν κολλᾶσθαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς· καὶ πάντες ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτόν, μὴ πιστεύοντες ὅτι ἐστὶν μαθητής.
records.gloss: Having arrived then in Jerusalem he was trying to join the disciples; and all were afraid of him, not believing that he is a disciple.
pieces: Once in Jerusalem, Saul made attempts to join the disciples, but every one of them feared him; they could not believe that he had become a disciple.

L.26: And having arrived in Jerusalem he was trying to join the disciples; and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

R.26: Saul came to Jerusalem. There he tried to join the group of Jesus's followers. But they were all afraid of him. They did not believe that he was really a follower of Jesus.

decisions.choice: arrived in Jerusalem: Paul's first visit after his call
alternatives: his return a few days later
decisions.reason: Paul says he went up to Jerusalem after three years to visit Cephas and stayed fifteen days (Galatians 1:18). Acts does not give the time.

decisions.choice: was trying: he tried again and again
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes repeated attempts that did not succeed.

decisions.choice: join: attach oneself to a group, become one of them
decisions.reason: The verb means to cling to or join closely (5:13, 10:28).

decisions.choice: the group of Jesus's followers; a follower of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a disciple is.

records.source: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶδεν τὸν κύριον καὶ ὅτι ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ καὶ πῶς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ἐπαρρησιάσατο ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: Barnabas however having taken hold of him brought [him] to the apostles and related to them how on the road he saw the Lord and that he spoke to him, and how in Damascus he spoke boldly in the name of Jesus.
pieces: Barnabas, however, took him in hand and brought him to the apostles. He explained to them that on the road Saul had seen the Lord, who had spoken to him, and that in Damascus Saul had spoken out without fear in the name of Jesus.

L.27: But Barnabas took hold of him [and] brought [him] to the apostles, and he described to them how on the road he had seen the Lord, and that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.

R.27: But Barnabas helped Saul. He took him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, and how the Lord had spoken to him. He also told them how Saul had spoken bravely about Jesus in Damascus.

decisions.choice: Barnabas: the Levite from Cyprus whose name means son of encouragement
decisions.reason: He was introduced in 4:36-37. Here he lives up to his name.

decisions.choice: he described: Barnabas; he had seen: Saul; he had spoken to him: the Lord
decisions.reason: The Greek uses "he" for three people. Barnabas is the subject of the sentence, so he is most likely the one who tells the apostles.

decisions.choice: the apostles: Acts speaks of the apostles as a group
decisions.reason: Paul says that on this visit he saw none of the other apostles except Cephas and James the Lord's brother (Galatians 1:18-19). Acts does not say which apostles were there.

decisions.choice: spoke boldly: spoke openly and without fear
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the apostles' preaching (4:13, 4:29, 4:31).

decisions.choice: Saul; the Lord
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the persons, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: spoken bravely about Jesus
alternatives: spoken boldly in the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what speaking in his name meant here.

records.source: καὶ ἦν μετ’ αὐτῶν εἰσπορευόμενος καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, παρρησιαζόμενος ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου, ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς· οἱ δὲ ἐπεχείρουν ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And he was with them coming in and going out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord, \v 29 he was speaking also and debating with the Hellenists; they however were trying to kill him.
pieces: From then on Saul was with them, going in and out among them in Jerusalem and speaking openly in the name of the Lord.
He spoke with the Greek-speaking Jews and argued with them, but they began making attempts on his life.

L.28: And he was with them, coming in and going out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord,
L.29: and he was speaking and debating with the Hellenists; but they were attempting to kill him.

R.28: So Saul stayed with the apostles and went everywhere with them in Jerusalem. He spoke bravely about the Lord Jesus.
R.29: He talked with the Jews who spoke Greek and argued with them. But they kept trying to kill him.

decisions.choice: coming in and going out: living and moving among them freely
decisions.reason: The same phrase describes Jesus's life among his followers in 1:21.

decisions.choice: the Hellenists: Greek-speaking Jews, here those who did not believe
decisions.reason: In 6:1 the word is used of Greek-speaking Jewish believers. In 6:9 Greek-speaking Jews from abroad argued with Stephen; now Saul, who had approved of Stephen's death (8:1), meets the same opposition.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: The verse repeats what 9:27 said of Damascus, where Saul spoke boldly in the name of Jesus.

decisions.choice: Greek-speaking Jews; the Jews who spoke Greek
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the name means, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus; the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names the persons meant.

records.source: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ κατήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν εἰς Ταρσόν.
records.gloss: Having learned [it] however the brothers brought down him to Caesarea and sent away him to Tarsus.
pieces: When the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} came to know of it, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him on his way to Tarsus.

L.30: But when the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} learned [of it], they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

R.30: The other believers found out about this. So they took Saul down to the city of Caesarea, on the coast. From there they sent him home to Tarsus.

decisions.choice: the brothers: the believers in Jerusalem, men and women
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is the common word for fellow believers in Acts (1:15, 6:3).

decisions.choice: brought him down to Caesarea: down from the hill country to the port on the coast
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands high in the hills, so one goes down from it. Caesarea was the harbor city where the Roman governor lived (8:40, 23:23-33). From there Saul could sail home.

decisions.choice: Tarsus: Saul's home city in Cilicia
decisions.reason: Saul was from Tarsus (9:11). Paul says that he then went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia (Galatians 1:21). Barnabas finds him there in 11:25.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word here means the believers as a whole, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the other believers; on the coast; home
decisions.reason: Readable says who the brothers were and what the places were to Saul.

records.source: Ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησία καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας εἶχεν εἰρήνην οἰκοδομουμένη, καὶ πορευομένη τῷ φόβῳ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῇ παρακλήσει τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐπληθύνετο.
records.gloss: The indeed then church throughout whole of Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up, and going on in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit it was multiplied.
pieces: So it was that the church across all of Judea, Galilee and Samaria had peace. It was being built up and walked in the fear of the Lord, and with the Holy Spirit's encouragement its numbers kept growing.

L.31: So then the church throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up; and going on in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, it was multiplied.

R.31: After this, the church everywhere in Judea, Galilee and Samaria had a time of peace. The church grew stronger. Its people lived with deep respect for the Lord. The Holy Spirit encouraged them, and more and more people joined the church.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the church", singular
alternatives: many later manuscripts read "the churches", with plural verbs
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts have the singular. Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("then had the churches rest"), have the plural throughout the sentence, perhaps to match 15:41 and 16:5. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the church: the believers of three regions seen as one church
decisions.reason: Acts usually speaks of the church in one place (8:1, 11:22, 13:1). Here, with the SBLGNT reading, the believers across Judea, Galilee and Samaria are one church.

decisions.choice: had peace: a time free from persecution
decisions.reason: The persecution that began with Stephen's death (8:1-3) has come to an end; its leader has become a believer.

decisions.choice: in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit: the first goes with how the church lived, the second with how it grew
alternatives: both go with how it lived
both go with how it grew
decisions.reason: The Greek phrases can be grouped in more than one way. The reading chosen follows the order of the words; the others are possible and change little.

decisions.choice: comfort: encouragement and help
decisions.reason: The word means being called alongside to help: encouragement, exhortation or comfort (compare 4:36, 13:15).

decisions.choice: walked
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to go or walk on a road; Balanced keeps the picture of a way of life.

decisions.choice: lived with deep respect for the Lord; more and more people joined the church
alternatives: going on in the fear of the Lord; was multiplied
decisions.reason: Readable says what the fear of the Lord is, and what the church's multiplying meant.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ Πέτρον διερχόμενον διὰ πάντων κατελθεῖν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἁγίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Λύδδα.
records.gloss: It came to pass now Peter passing through all [places] to come down also to the holy ones those dwelling in Lydda.
pieces: Peter was traveling about through the whole area, and he came down to visit the holy people living in Lydda.

L.32: Now it happened that Peter, going through all [the regions], came down also to the holy ones who lived in Lydda.

R.32: Peter was traveling from place to place. He went to visit the holy people who lived in the town of Lydda.

decisions.choice: passing through all: going through all the regions just named
alternatives: going around among all the believers
decisions.reason: The word for "all" has no noun. It may mean the regions of 9:31 or all the believers; either way Peter is visiting the churches.

decisions.choice: Lydda: a town on the coastal plain, north-west of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Lydda lay on the road from Jerusalem to Joppa, about twenty-five miles from Jerusalem and some ten miles from Joppa (9:38). It is the Lod of 1 Chronicles 8:12.

decisions.choice: holy ones: the believers
decisions.reason: As in 9:13.

decisions.choice: holy people
decisions.reason: As in 9:13.

records.heading: Aeneas is healed at Lydda

records.source: εὗρεν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπόν τινα ὀνόματι Αἰνέαν ἐξ ἐτῶν ὀκτὼ κατακείμενον ἐπὶ κραβάττου, ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος.
records.gloss: He found then there a man certain by name Aeneas, for years eight lying on a mat, who was paralyzed.
pieces: There he came upon a man called Aeneas, a paralyzed man who had been confined to his bed for eight years.

L.33: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been lying on a mat for eight years, who was paralyzed.

R.33: There he met a man named Aeneas. Aeneas was paralyzed. He had not been able to get out of bed for eight years.

decisions.choice: for eight years
alternatives: since he was eight years old
decisions.reason: The phrase most often gives how long something has lasted (compare Luke 8:43). It can also mean from a certain age.

decisions.choice: mat: a light bed or pallet
decisions.reason: The word is used of the poor man's bed, easy to carry (5:15; Mark 2:4).

decisions.choice: Aeneas: a Greek name
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether he was a believer, though Peter had come to visit the believers (9:32).

decisions.choice: not able to get out of bed
decisions.reason: Readable says what lying on a mat for years meant.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Αἰνέα, ἰᾶταί σε Ἰησοῦς Χριστός· ἀνάστηθι καὶ στρῶσον σεαυτῷ· καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέστη.
records.gloss: And said to him the Peter, Aeneas, heals you Jesus Christ; rise up and spread [it] for yourself. And immediately he rose up.
pieces: Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is healing you. Get up and make your bed." He got up at once.

L.34: And Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} heals you. Rise up and spread [your bed] for yourself." And immediately he rose up.

R.34: Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is making you well. Get up and make your bed yourself." Right away Aeneas got up.

decisions.choice: Jesus Christ heals you: Jesus, not Peter, does the healing
alternatives: Peter heals in his own power
decisions.reason: Peter said the same of the lame man (3:12, 3:16, 4:10).

decisions.choice: heals: is healing you now
decisions.reason: The present tense says the healing is happening as Peter speaks.

decisions.choice: spread for yourself: make your own bed
alternatives: get a couch ready for a meal
decisions.reason: The verb means to spread. It can mean to make a bed, or to spread couches for eating (Mark 14:15). Either way Aeneas will now do for himself what others did for him.

decisions.choice: [your bed]
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; Literal supplies the likely one in brackets.

records.source: καὶ εἶδαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες Λύδδα καὶ τὸν Σαρῶνα, οἵτινες ἐπέστρεψαν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
records.gloss: And saw him all those inhabiting Lydda and the Sharon, who turned to the Lord.
pieces: Everyone living in Lydda and the plain of Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.

L.35: And all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, who turned to the Lord.

R.35: All the people who lived in Lydda and in the area of Sharon saw him healed. So they turned to the Lord and began to follow {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Sharon: the coastal plain north of Lydda and Joppa
decisions.reason: The plain of Sharon runs along the coast toward Mount Carmel (Isaiah 35:2; 1 Chronicles 27:29).

decisions.choice: turned to the Lord: turned from their old life to believe in Jesus
decisions.reason: Acts uses the phrase for coming to faith (11:21, 15:19, 26:20).

decisions.choice: all: a large response, said in general terms
decisions.reason: Luke uses "all" for a wide response, as in 9:42 "many" believed.

decisions.choice: and they turned
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the relative clause a main clause.

decisions.choice: saw him healed; began to follow him
alternatives: saw him; turned to the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says what they saw and what turning to the Lord meant.

records.source: Ἐν Ἰόππῃ δέ τις ἦν μαθήτρια ὀνόματι Ταβιθά, ἣ διερμηνευομένη λέγεται Δορκάς· αὕτη ἦν πλήρης ἔργων ἀγαθῶν καὶ ἐλεημοσυνῶν ὧν ἐποίει.
records.gloss: In Joppa now a certain there was disciple by name Tabitha, which being translated is called Dorcas; this [woman] was full of works good and of alms which she was doing.
pieces: At Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha; translated, the name is Dorcas, which means gazelle. Her days were full of good works and of the gifts she gave to the poor.

L.36: Now in Joppa there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which translated is Dorcas. She was full of good works and of acts of charity which she kept doing.

R.36: In the town of Joppa there was a woman named Tabitha who followed Jesus. In Greek her name was Dorcas. Both names mean "gazelle." She always did good things for others and gave to poor people.

decisions.choice: Tabitha, Dorcas: her name in Aramaic and in Greek; both mean gazelle
decisions.reason: Tabitha is the Aramaic word for a gazelle, and Dorcas the Greek word. Luke translates the name for readers who know Greek, and uses both names in 9:39-40.

decisions.choice: disciple: a woman disciple
decisions.reason: The word is the feminine form of disciple, used only here in the New Testament. She is counted among the disciples as fully as the men.

decisions.choice: acts of charity: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: The word means mercy shown in giving; it is used of gifts to the poor (3:2-3, 10:2, 10:4).

decisions.choice: which she kept doing: her habit of life
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes what she did again and again; 9:39 shows the clothing she made.

decisions.choice: Joppa: the port on the coast, today Jaffa
decisions.reason: Joppa was the harbor from which Jonah sailed (Jonah 1:3). It lay on the coast north-west of Lydda (9:38).

decisions.choice: which means gazelle; both names mean gazelle
decisions.reason: Luke gives the translation because the meaning was clear to his readers; Balanced and Readable add the meaning for readers today, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: a woman who followed Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a disciple is.

records.heading: Tabitha is raised at Joppa

records.source: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἀσθενήσασαν αὐτὴν ἀποθανεῖν· λούσαντες δὲ ἔθηκαν αὐτὴν ἐν ὑπερῴῳ.
records.gloss: It came to pass however in the days those having become sick her to die; having washed [her] then they laid her in an upper room.
pieces: Just at that time she fell ill and died. They washed her body and laid it in an upper room.

L.37: And it happened in those days that she fell sick and died; and having washed [her], they laid her in an upper room.

R.37: At that time she got sick and died. Some people washed her body. Then they put it in a room upstairs.

decisions.choice: washed her: the usual washing of a body before burial
alternatives: a ritual for bringing back to life
decisions.reason: The dead were washed and prepared for burial, which usually followed soon after death.

decisions.choice: laid her in an upper room: not buried at once
alternatives: the usual place to lay out the dead
decisions.reason: Laying her upstairs, and sending for Peter (9:38), may show that the disciples hoped for more than comfort. The text does not say what they hoped.

decisions.choice: in those days: while Peter was at Lydda
decisions.reason: The phrase ties her death to Peter's stay nearby (9:32-35, 9:38).

decisions.choice: her body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say it was her body they washed.

records.source: ἐγγὺς δὲ οὔσης Λύδδας τῇ Ἰόππῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Πέτρος ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτῇ ἀπέστειλαν δύο ἄνδρας πρὸς αὐτὸν παρακαλοῦντες· Μὴ ὀκνήσῃς διελθεῖν ἕως ἡμῶν·
records.gloss: Near now being Lydda to Joppa, the disciples having heard that Peter is in it sent two men to him imploring, Not you should delay to come through to us.
pieces: Lydda was not far from Joppa, and when the disciples heard that Peter was there, they sent two men to him with the plea, "Please come to us without delay."

L.38: Now since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, having heard that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging, "Do not delay to come to us."

R.38: The town of Lydda was near Joppa. The followers of Jesus in Joppa heard that Peter was in Lydda. So they sent two men to him. The men begged Peter, "Please come to us quickly!"

decisions.choice: Lydda was near Joppa: about ten miles apart
decisions.reason: The two towns were a few hours' walk from each other, so Peter could come the same day.

decisions.choice: do not delay: an urgent but polite request
decisions.reason: The form is a prohibition, but from those asking a favor it is a plea.

decisions.choice: urging: begging, pleading
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to comfort or to urge; here it is an urgent request.

decisions.choice: please
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the pleading in the request itself.

decisions.choice: the followers of Jesus in Joppa
decisions.reason: Readable says who the disciples were.

records.source: ἀναστὰς δὲ Πέτρος συνῆλθεν αὐτοῖς· ὃν παραγενόμενον ἀνήγαγον εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον, καὶ παρέστησαν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ χῆραι κλαίουσαι καὶ ἐπιδεικνύμεναι χιτῶνας καὶ ἱμάτια ὅσα ἐποίει μετ’ αὐτῶν οὖσα ἡ Δορκάς.
records.gloss: Having risen up then Peter went with them; whom having arrived they brought up into the upper room, and stood by him all the widows weeping and showing tunics and garments, as many as was making with them being the Dorcas.
pieces: Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him up to the upper room. All the widows stood around him in tears, holding up the tunics and cloaks Dorcas would make when she was among them.

L.39: So Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they brought [him] up into the upper room, and all the widows stood beside him, weeping and showing tunics and garments, as many as Dorcas used to make while she was with them.

R.39: So Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him upstairs to the room. All the widows stood around Peter, crying. They showed him the shirts and coats Dorcas had made while she was alive.

decisions.choice: the widows: women without husbands, many of them poor
decisions.reason: Widows often had no one to provide for them; the church cared for them (6:1). Dorcas's gifts had clothed them.

decisions.choice: showing: holding up the clothes, or showing the ones they were wearing
decisions.reason: The verb is in the middle form, which can mean showing on oneself. The widows may have been wearing the clothes Dorcas made.

decisions.choice: tunics and garments: the garment worn next to the body and the outer cloak
decisions.reason: The same pair is used in Luke 6:29.

decisions.choice: as many as Dorcas used to make while she was with them
alternatives: what she made on one occasion
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes her habit; "while she was with them" means while she was alive.

decisions.choice: shirts and coats
decisions.reason: Readable uses common words for the two kinds of clothing.

records.source: ἐκβαλὼν δὲ ἔξω πάντας ὁ Πέτρος καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύξατο, καὶ ἐπιστρέψας πρὸς τὸ σῶμα εἶπεν· Ταβιθά, ἀνάστηθι.
records.gloss: Having put out then outside all the Peter and having placed the knees he prayed, and having turned to the body he said, Tabitha, rise up.
pieces: Peter made everyone leave the room. He knelt and prayed, then turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, stand up."

L.40: But Peter put them all outside, and kneeling down he prayed; and turning to the body he said, "Tabitha, rise up."

R.40: Peter told everyone to leave the room. He knelt down and prayed. Then he turned to the dead woman and said, "Tabitha, get up!"

decisions.choice: put them all outside; Tabitha, rise up: as Jesus raised Jairus's daughter
decisions.reason: Jesus put the mourners outside and said to the girl, "Talitha, koum", "little girl, get up" (Mark 5:40-41; Luke 8:51-54). Elijah and Elisha also prayed alone over the dead (1 Kings 17:19-22; 2 Kings 4:33).

decisions.choice: kneeling, he prayed
decisions.reason: Standing was a usual posture for prayer; kneeling marks earnest prayer (7:60, 20:36, 21:5).

decisions.choice: turning to the body: Peter prays first, then speaks to her
decisions.reason: Peter does not act in his own power; he asks God before he speaks.

decisions.choice: the dead woman
decisions.reason: Readable uses a gentler, clearer phrase.

records.source: ἡ δὲ ἤνοιξεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον ἀνεκάθισεν.
records.gloss: She then opened the eyes of her, and having seen the Peter she sat up.
pieces: She opened her eyes, and at the sight of Peter she sat up.

L.40: And she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter she sat up.

R.40: Tabitha opened her eyes. When she saw Peter, she sat up.

decisions.choice: she opened her eyes and sat up: as in earlier raisings of the dead
decisions.reason: The boy Elisha raised opened his eyes (2 Kings 4:35), and the young man Jesus raised at Nain sat up (Luke 7:15).

decisions.choice: Tabitha
decisions.reason: Readable names her.

records.source: δοὺς δὲ αὐτῇ χεῖρα ἀνέστησεν αὐτήν, φωνήσας δὲ τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ τὰς χήρας παρέστησεν αὐτὴν ζῶσαν.
records.gloss: Having given then to her a hand he raised up her; having called then the holy ones and the widows he presented her living.
pieces: Peter gave her his hand and raised her up. Then he called in the holy people and the widows and presented her to them, alive.

L.41: And giving her [his] hand, he raised her up; and calling the holy ones and the widows, he presented her alive.

R.41: Peter took her hand and helped her stand up. Then he called the holy people and the widows back into the room. He showed them that Tabitha was alive.

decisions.choice: raised her up: helped her to her feet
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for rising from the dead, and here it is used in its plain sense of helping someone stand. The raising itself has already happened (9:40).

decisions.choice: the holy ones and the widows: the believers, with the widows named among them
decisions.reason: The widows were believers too; Luke names them because they mourned her most (9:39).

decisions.choice: alive: living again
decisions.reason: The word means living. She had died (9:37).

decisions.choice: holy people
decisions.reason: As in 9:13.

records.source: γνωστὸν δὲ ἐγένετο καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰόππης, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
records.gloss: Known then it became throughout whole of Joppa, and believed many on the Lord.
pieces: Word of this went all through Joppa, and many came to believe in the Lord.

L.42: And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

R.42: People all over Joppa heard about what had happened. Many of them believed in the Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: believed in the Lord: put their trust in the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: The phrase means trusting oneself to the Lord, as in 11:17 and 16:31, where the Lord is named as Jesus.

decisions.choice: believed: came to believe
decisions.reason: The aorist marks the moment of coming to faith.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the Lord, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ἐγένετο δὲ ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς μεῖναι ἐν Ἰόππῃ παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ.
records.gloss: It came to pass then days many to remain him in Joppa with a certain Simon a tanner.
pieces: Peter stayed on in Joppa for many days, as the guest of one Simon, a tanner.

L.43: And it happened that he stayed many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.

R.43: Peter stayed in Joppa for many days. He lived at the house of a man named Simon, who made leather from animal skins.

decisions.choice: a tanner: one who made leather from animal hides
decisions.reason: Tanning used the skins of dead animals and was a smelly trade. 10:6 says Simon's house was by the sea. The text does not comment on Peter's staying with him.

decisions.choice: many days: a good while
decisions.reason: Luke uses the phrase for a stay of some length (9:23). The story of Cornelius begins while Peter is there (10:5-6).

decisions.choice: who made leather from animal skins
decisions.reason: Readable explains the trade.
